Shri Sourabh Neema, learned counsel for the appella
 Shri Sudhir Dandwate, learned counsel for the respo
 Order

The appellants have filed this appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act being aggrieved by the award dated 20.12.2008 passed in claim case No.119/2007 challenging the quantum of compensation on the ground of inadequate assessment of income of the deceased.
2. The liability of insurance company due to death in accident by the insured vehicle is not under dispute.

3. The short facts of the case are that on 13.07.2006 the deceased Ajay Yadav had gone by scooty of his younger brother registration No. MP09-JD- 7841 for refilling petrol at Malviya Petrol Pump,
Ring Road.

At around 7 p.m. when he reached near Karan Guarden, respondent No.2 came driving Eicher bus registration No.MP09-K-1583 in a rash and negligent manner from the side of Khajrana square without giving indication and dashed into scooty of Ajay because of which he fell down and sustained grievous 2 MA-1078-2009 injuries.
He was rushed to Bombay Hospital but while on the way he died.
4. The appellants filed claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act and claimed compensation for the death of Ajay.

The claims tribunal after considering the evidence on record awarded a total compensation of Rs.6,39,500/- out of which an amount of Rs.6,20,000/- was for loss of dependency and rest of the amount was under different conventional heads.

5. Learned counsel for the appellants submits that the claims tribunal while considering the evidence regarding income of the deceased though believed that the deceased was operating business of running a boys hostel, however, the claim regarding income of the deceased at Rs.1,39,786/- per annum has been disbelieved and on notional basis his income was taken at Rs.5000/- per month.

By referring to Ex.P-12 i.e. income tax return, he submits that the income of the deceased was Rs.1,39,786/-, thus, the said amount should have been taken as annual income of Smt.Nootan Yadav & Ors. vs M/S Ayashar Moters Ltd. & Ors.

sentences.text: 6. The learned counsel contends that it is settled by the Apex Court in various pronouncements that the income tax return being statutory documents should not be discarded by the claims tribunal.
He further submits that in the case of Nidhi Bhargava (supra) the circumstances were somewhat similar.
In that case also the return was filed after the death of the deceased.
The Hon'ble Apex Court observed in para 12 that only for the reason that return was filed after the death of the deceased, the same cannot be discarded.
He thus prays for reassessing income of the deceased for quantifying compensation for loss of dependency by taking his income at Rs.1,39,786/-.

Apart from this he also argued that no amount for future prospects has been awarded by the claims tribunal which is not sustainable in view of the law as laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi and others,
2017 (16) SCC 680.

entities.text:
National Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Pranay Sethi and others,
2017 (16) SCC 680
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He further stresses upon the fact that for loss of consortium Rs.10,000/- each has been awarded to four claimants whereas in view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Pranay Sethi (supra), the amount should have been Rs.40000/- each.

Apart from this,
he also submits that an amount of Rs.2000 and 2500/- has been awarded for funeral expenses and loss of estate which is not adequate amount of compensation.

Apart from the award of compensation in different heads, he also points out that even while assessing the income of the deceased 1/3rd has been deducted whereas in view of law laid down in the case of Sarla Verma and others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another, AIR 2009 Supreme Court 3104 and Pranay Sethi (supra), looking to four members as dependents 1/4th should have been deducted from the income of the deceased for personal expenses.

entities.text: Sarla Verma and others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another, AIR 2009 Supreme Court 3104
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, he prays for enhancement of compensation.

7. Per contra, learned counsel for the insurance company points out that the claims tribunal has considered the evidence regarding income of the 4 MA-1078-2009 deceased in para 17 of the award and after discussing the statement of witness Nemichand Choukse PW-3 and the documents adduced in evidence the claims tribunal has clearly recorded in said para that the witness is not trustworthy.
Thus, the evidence regarding income has been discarded by the claims tribunal.
He thus submits that the claim regarding income has correctly been discarded by the claims tribunal.
He further points out that in the cases cited by the counsel for the appellants the facts were different inasmuch as in those cases there were already income tax returns filed for previous years.

In this view of the matter, Hon'ble the Apex Court observed that only for the reason of filing of income tax return for the relevant year subsequent to death of the deceased the same cannot be discarded.

As regards the fact of the present case, he relied upon the order passed by this Court in the case of Suchitra Sinha and others Vs. Baijnath and others, 2006 ACJ 2317 as well as Sutinder Pal Singh Arora and others Vs. Ashok Kumar Jain and others, 2004 ACJ 2004 782 and submits that in those cases also for the same reasons income tax returns have been discarded by the Court as they were filed subsequent to death of the deceased.
8.

sentences.text: From the perusal of Ex.P-15 and Ex.P-16 it would come to the fore that exhibits contain details regarding students who were paying rent, however, this list of details cannot be taken as income of the deceased.

As regards the income tax return Ex.P-12 although it shows that the income of the deceased was Rs.1,39,687/-, however, not only that this return was filed after the death of the deceased but if the same is seen in juxtaposition to the statement given 5 MA-1078-2009 by the wife of the deceased PW-1 then her claim of income of the deceased at Rs.14000/- per month does not match with the details of income tax return.

Thus, in the considered view of this Court, not only that the return was filed subsequent to death of the deceased but it contradicts the claim made by the wife of the deceased, thus, the claims tribunal has rightly disbelieved the same.
However, in para No.21 of the impugned award the claims tribunal has concluded that the deceased was found to be operating the business of running boys hostel.
There is no challenge to the findings of the claims tribunal.
As such the deceased has to be treated a person who was conducting business at the time of his death and for this reason, his income at Rs.5000/- per month appears to be very less.
10. In the considered view of this Court, the income of the deceased considering that there are receipts of rent of Rs.8000/- per month has to be taken as Rs.8000/- per month.
Considering his age at 35 years, addition of 40% has to be made in the income of the head of future prospects and commensurate to his age multiplier of 16 has to be applied.
Apart from this, indisputably there are 4 dependents of the deceased thus deduction from his income for personal expenses has to be made at 1/4th.

After applying these parameters, the total compensation for the loss of dependency would come to Rs.16,12,800/- and looking to the fact that the claimants are wife, children and mother, four in numbers, the amount of Rs.40,000/- each is awarded to all of four of them totaling to Rs.1,60,000/-.
For loss of estate and funeral expenses, Rs.15000/- each is awarded.
Hence, the total compensation now comes to Rs.18,02,800/-.

After deducting the amount of Rs.6,89,500/-
6 MA-1078-2009 already awarded by the claims tribunal, the enhanced amount of Rs.11,39,300/-
has to be paid over and above the amount already awarded by the claims tribunal.
This enhanced amount shall carry interest @6% per annum from the date of application before the claims tribunal.
11. With the aforesaid, the present appeal stands allowed.

(PAVAN KUMAR DWIVEDI) JUDGE N.R.
